findings.message: In the controller route's `reuse` branch of `frame()`, a `checkTime()` deadline check performed after `reuseAssessment` resolves is inside the same `try` as the reuse call, so if the deadline expires there it falls into the generic `catch` and is recorded via `taskFailure(..., false)` ('failed'), rather than the timeout-aware classification ('incomplete') the equivalent daemon-route reuse path in `coordinator.ts` gives via its `timeout` sentinel check.

tasks.summary: Fresh (reassessed) review of S2/t3: the history-aware reassess/reuse engine across both actual reviewer parties. I independently fetched the exact pinned content of all 12 in-scope files via `git show 2b1eb55b9:<path>` and confirmed each is byte-identical to the embedded reviewed-version blocks (assessment.ts, contracts.ts, controller.ts, coordinator.ts, packet.ts, policy.ts, publication.ts, record.ts, results.ts, and the three test/fixture files). Tracing the logic: `ReassessmentSchema`/`reviewAssignments` validate attempt>1 attribution into reassess/reuse decisions; `sourceAssessment`/`reuseAssessment` resolve an earlier same-party attempt's task result and re-run it through `assessTaskResult`→`normalizeTaskResult`, then assert `isDeepStrictEqual` against the original — a strong idempotence check that both proves the source is replayed verbatim and forbids silent rewriting (confirmed against the 'reuse decisions' test's missing/duplicate/foreign/rewritten/foreign-party/cycle-guard negative cases, all of which I traced to the exact `requireReview` guard that rejects them). `validateResultOrigins` enforces strictly-decreasing same-party unchanged-result ancestry on live and persisted CR bodies alike, ruling out cycles by construction. Both `controller.ts`'s `scope()`/`expire()` and `coordinator.ts`'s per-task catch block implement equivalent parity for attribution-validation-failure ('failed') vs attribution-timeout ('incomplete') across the daemon and controller adapters — I traced both branches line-by-line and confirmed this is deliberate symmetric behavior, not a defect. `assignmentPrompt`/`attributionPrompt` embed the full relevant prior feedback + reassessment decision + checkpoint path inline with no added model turn (confirmed via the 'history prompts' and 'sequential re-review' tests' call counts: 2 total daemon-side calls, 0 controller-side calls). `codeTaskCommands` applies the whitespace-injection guard consistently at every grant site including the two new ones (the submitted-evidence loop, already constrained by a strict charset regex, and the new 'prior pinned context' loop, which has an explicit `!/\s/.test(reference)` check). `record.ts`'s `renderTaskReview` correctly walks the reuse chain back to the true original attempt/reviewer via its `while(earlier)` loop (traced against the 'CR provenance' test's two-hop reuse scenario and its exact regex assertion). I ran all 5 named test cases in `history.test.ts` directly and they passed (5/5); I also ran a project-wide `tsc --noEmit`, which was clean. I overturn attempt 1's one LOW finding (policy.ts:49) after fresh inspection: it argued the prompt's claim that `review.path` is reachable 'through the existing read tools' is unsupported because `codeTaskCommands()` never grants that literal path. That is true of `codeTaskCommands` in isolation, but it is not the only grant surface — `src/agent/providers/cli-provider.ts`'s `claudeReviewSessionArgs` always grants `REVIEW_SESSION_READ_TOOLS = ['Read','Grep','Glob']` unconditionally (no path restriction) to a reviewer session, independent of `codeTaskCommands` (which only gates the `Bash` tool). So the prompt's claim is factually accurate, and I do not carry the LOW finding forward. No HIGH/MED findings resulted from my own inspection.
